title: APA § 706(1): discrete action legally required
summary: A court can compel a specific action the agency must take, including an overdue required decision, while leaving discretionary substantive choices to the agency.
notes:
Norton requires both discreteness and legal obligation. Identifying a mandatory broad statutory goal does not identify a discrete step that the agency must perform. Conversely, identifying a precise desirable step does not establish that the law requires it. A statutory deadline for a decision can support compulsion even though the agency retains authority to decide its substance.

The supplied land-planning notes distinguish challenges to concrete actions inconsistent with an adopted plan from demands to enforce the plan’s projections. They report later agency efforts to describe plans as strategic and aspirational, illustrating how review doctrines can influence agencies’ drafting and planning practices. They also introduce finality, ripeness, and exhaustion as separate timing constraints. This excerpt supplies only that introduction; it does not provide the full later timing chapter. The preceding fragment reports that the Farmworker Justice Fund opinion was withdrawn as moot after OSHA issued a sanitation standard; the fragment does not supply the original opinion’s complete analysis.
